Reading the room

  • Your two pendants are the constraint nobody mentions. They hang in a line, spaced for a long table. A round table wants to sit centred under a single light. Either centre the circle under the nearer pendant and accept the second one lighting nothing, or move one — the cable is looped at the ceiling rose in the photo, so there is slack to play with.
  • Ø120 is the honest four-seater. Ø100 seats four only if the base is a single stem or pedestal. Anything with four corner legs at Ø100 is a two-seater with ambitions.
  • Match the floor or contrast it, do not near-miss it. The laminate is a pale grey-toned oak. Acacia, walnut and brown-stained oak all read warmer and redder — they work as a deliberate contrast. A light oak veneer that is one shade off reads as a mistake.
  • The pendants are black, and nothing else in the room is. A table with a black frame or column (SKOGSTA, MARIEDAMM, STENSELE) is the only thing that would answer them.
  • Sklum ships from Spain. Prices are keen and the cement and travertine-look tops are genuinely distinctive, but check the delivery window and the return terms before committing — several pieces on this page are on back-order.
Prices, stock and availability read live on Saturday 29 August 2026 from the IKEA UK catalogue and stock API, and from Sklum UK product data. Habitat prices are marked check price where they could not be read: habitat.co.uk and argos.co.uk block automated requests entirely, so the Habitat entries carry names, sizes and photographs but only one confirmed price. Everything here is a snapshot and will drift — follow the links for the live figure.

Diameters are as published by each retailer. Where a table is listed as extendable, the diameter given is the closed, round size.
